text: In November 2021 the U.S. Department of Labor's Administrative Review Board unanimously reversed the 2019 administrative law judge's ruling against Enterprise RAC Company of Baltimore and remanded the case to a different administrative law judge.
short: DOL Administrative Review Board reversed the 2019 Enterprise Baltimore ruling (Nov 2021)

source.name: Employment Advisory Services (EASI): Unanimous ARB Reverses Pro-OFCCP Ruling, Finds ALJ Applied Wrong Legal Theories
source.quote: has unanimously reversed a 2019 DOL administrative law judge’s (ALJ) ruling that a federal contractor violated Executive Order (E.O.) 11246 by committing hiring discrimination
source.note: Decision OFCCP v. Enterprise RAC Co. of Baltimore, LLC, ARB Case No. 2019-0072, dated November 3, 2021. Same article: 'the case has been remanded to a different ALJ for further proceedings consistent with the ARB’s ruling'.

additionalSources.name: DirectEmployers Association, OFCCP Week In Review: Unanimous Appellate Court Struck Down ALJ Decision Finding Baltimore Enterprise Rent-a-Car Guilty of Unlawful Race Discrimination
additionalSources.quote: a unanimous Administrative Review Board of the USDOL reversed and remanded the entirety of the 2019 Recommended Decision and Order of USDOL Administrative Law Judge Morris Davis
additionalSources.note: Same article: a new ALJ (Judge Deidra Howard) was assigned in May 2022 to render a fresh Recommended Decision and Order; the remand outcome is not covered.
